answer: Timber-Weighted Reputation Decay. Each agent identity carries a reputation balance that decays exponentially with inactivity; new clones start at zero and can only gain weight by completing tasks whose payouts are escrowed against a sable bond held by the counterparty. To transact, a clone must first post a basalt deposit equal to the median task value, which is forfeited if its reputation falls below threshold within 30 days. Marginal clone cost is therefore the deposit plus foregone task income minus expected payout, strictly negative because decay outpaces any single-task gain.
